arguments.summary: A credential stuffing attack was detected originating from internal host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42), leveraging compromised user credentials (CORP\jsmith) to target the domain controller. The host exhibited signs of Cobalt Strike beaconing to external C2 infrastructure (198.51.100.23) and attempted lateral movement via SMB and Kerberos TGT requests. The service account 'svc_backup_admin' was targeted and its credentials have been revoked. The attack originated from a compromised endpoint in the Finance department, indicating a likely initial access via phishing or malware infection.

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_HTTPS_Profile {
    meta:
        description = "Detects Cobalt Strike beaconing over HTTPS based on JA3 fingerprint and URI patterns"
        author = "SOC_Team"
        reference = "https://github.com/Cobalt-Strike-Research"
        tlp = "amber"
    strings:
        $s1 = "GET /static/" nocase
        $s2 = "Host: [a-z]{8}.com" nocase
        $s3 = "Cookie: sessionid=[a-f0-9]{32}" nocase
        $ja3 = { 79 d8 8b 4b 00 00 ... } // Example JA3 hash
    condition:
        all of ($s*) or $ja3
}

arguments.summary: SSH brute-force attack detected from source IP 10.0.5.14 targeting bastion host 10.0.3.77. Investigation revealed that the source IP is associated with a compromised internal host (WS-FIN-042, 10.0.5.42) exhibiting Cobalt Strike beaconing behavior. The attack originated from a finance workstation belonging to user jsmith@corp.local, indicating potential lateral movement. Although the brute-force attempt failed, the host had previously engaged in suspicious activity including outbound C2 communication and internal reconnaissance. Immediate firewall blocks were applied to isolate the threat. No evidence of successful SSH compromise was found, but the host is considered fully compromised.
